corridor.title: Green Corridor

intro.heading: Green Corridor cost model
intro.body: Evaluate a green shipping corridor: the NPV cost gap between running it on green fuel versus fossil fuel, with EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, IRA 45Z and custom regulation layered on top. Fill in the five steps — each covers one area of the model — and read the results in the always-visible panel. Benchmarks fill every field; override only what you know better.

routeMap.indicative: indicative route - maritime network, screening grade
routeMap.placeholder: Set port coordinates on the Ports tab to draw the sailing route.

viewMode.label: View mode
viewMode.hiddenActive: {count, plural, one {# detailed setting} other {# detailed settings}} in effect but hidden in Simplified view.
viewMode.upgradeConfirm: Switching this project to Standard is permanent - it unlocks every field and cannot be undone. Continue?

cargo.waccHelp: Benchmarked by country — override with a project-specific cost of capital. The country table is illustrative, not a verified source.
cargo.countryHelp: The corridor's anchor country — port A's country — selects the financing (WACC) benchmark. Denmark, Netherlands, India, Brazil, Singapore and the United States carry their own reference benchmarks; every other country uses the generic benchmark. Ports and the second country are descriptive.
cargo.unitWeightHelp: What one cargo unit weighs. TEU defaults to 10 t; tonne is 1 by definition. Used to derive cost per tonne of cargo; the model itself counts units.
cargo.routedHelp: Routed over the maritime shipping-lane network ({graph}), {via}, one-way. Indicative - screening grade, within roughly 5-10% of published tables.
cargo.routedDivergence: Typed distance differs from the routed route by {pct}% - the network gives {nm} nm, {via}.
cargo.portBCoordsHelp: With Port A's coordinates, these let the corridor route over the maritime shipping-lane network - the drawing and the routed distance benchmark.
cargo.portCoordsHelp: Functional for build-here: the plant→port logistics leg computes from these coordinates. Leave untouched otherwise.
cargo.routeTypeHelp: Point-to-point compares two named ports; single point anchors the corridor at one port when the far end is not decided yet. It only controls whether the second port's details appear below.
cargo.startYearHelp: The year the corridor starts operating. Regulation phases in over time (ETS coverage, FuelEU targets), so a later start meets stricter rules from day one.
cargo.horizonHelp: How many years of operation the comparison covers. Costs are summed over this window, so a longer horizon gives fuel bills and support schemes more years to weigh against the up-front ships.
cargo.portNameHelp: A display name for this port. It labels the map and exports — it does not change any cost.
cargo.unitsHelp: How many cargo units the corridor delivers per year. Ships and roundtrips drive the costs, so this mainly sets the denominator of cost per unit shipped.
cargo.unitHelp: What one unit of cargo is — a tonne, or a TEU container. It names the per-unit figures; choosing TEU reveals the weight per container.
cargo.inflationHelp: How fast costs rise each year. Future fuel, crew and maintenance bills grow at this rate before discounting brings them back to today's money.
cargo.distanceHelp: The one-way sailing distance between the ports, in nautical miles. It drives the fuel burned per roundtrip - the dominant physical lever in the model. Once both ports have coordinates, the routed shipping-lane distance is offered for adoption.

vessel.type: Vessel type (same class for both fleets)
vessel.energyBasis: Energy use {gj} GJ/nm, measured at {kn} kn service speed. Steaming slower burns less per mile (roughly with the square of speed); the figure is meaningless without the speed it was measured at.
vessel.portShare: Port and cargo-system energy is {pct}% of a round trip, assuming {days} port days. Negligible on a corridor this long.
vessel.portShareWarn: Port and cargo-system energy is {pct}% of a round trip, assuming {days} port days — a material share on a corridor this short. These day rates are sector estimates, not sourced figures, so this scenario leans on the least-evidenced part of the vessel data.
vessel.capexGreenHelp: Per-ship figure, multiplied by the vessel count for the fleet total. Benchmark = vessel type × (1 + green-fuel readiness premium), the same single-hull basis — so restoring the benchmark no longer changes the dimension.
vessel.capexFossilHelp: Per-ship figure, multiplied by the vessel count. Benchmark 0 — existing baseline fleet, so no newbuild capital; override when the comparison builds new fossil tonnage too.
vessel.typeHelp: The ship class both sides of the comparison sail. It sets the energy needed per nautical mile and the benchmark price and running cost per ship — the single most decisive choice in the model.
vessel.vesselsHelp: How many ships the corridor runs. Every ship adds its full purchase and running cost on both sides, and together with roundtrips it sets how much fuel is burned.
vessel.roundtripsHelp: Voyages per ship per year. More roundtrips burn more fuel without adding ships, shifting the cost balance from capital toward fuel.
vessel.opexHelp: The yearly cost of running one ship — crew, maintenance, insurance — before fuel. Fuel is priced separately from consumption and fuel price.

fuel.sourcingSimplifiedNote: This project sources fuel from a built plant - a Standard capability. Upgrade to Standard to change the sourcing mode; the numbers keep computing exactly as saved.
fuel.sourcingBuildHere: Build here (pick a site on the map)
fuel.wtwHelp: Effective well-to-wake intensity the model uses. Under refined accounting (v6) it DERIVES from the fuel-emissions dataset - certified pathway + slip + pilot on the green side, the framework's row on the fossil side; on legacy scenarios it is the workbook benchmark. Override only to pin a custom value.
fuel.consumptionHelp: Benchmark from the vessel type, or derived from distance when selected in the Vessel step.
fuel.prodOpex: Fuel production O&M, excl. fuel purchase
fuel.prodZeroNote: Forced to 0 under this sourcing — production cost lives inside the fuel price.
fuel.legacyPriceNote: Legacy accounting: this merchant price is charged ON TOP of the production CAPEX/O&M below.
fuel.certifiedWttHelp: The green fuel's certified well-to-tank E-value from the Proof of Sustainability, gCO2e/MJ. Never zero - a zero pathway is an assumption, not a certifiable value. Prefilled with the dataset's reference default for this fuel; combustion terms (N2O slip, pilot) are added on top by the model.
fuel.n2oScenarioHelp: THE dominant uncertainty in ammonia's profile: published values span x37 and neither framework fixes a default. Three cited scenarios from the fuel-emissions dataset; the default is the optimised-injection literature value.
fuel.pilotShareHelp: Dual-fuel engines burn a fossil pilot for ignition - around 5% of energy (MAN ES / WinGD). Its emissions ride the green side's derived factors; its energy is not added to the tonnage bookkeeping (documented approximation).
fuel.sulphurHelp: Mass % sulphur. The IMO bins residual fuels by sulphur (MEPC.391(81)): 0.10-0.50% carries WtT 16.8 gCO2e/MJ, above 0.50% carries 14.1. Only consulted under IMO accounting.
fuel.typeHelp: The fuel this side burns. Its price benchmark, energy content and emission factors travel with it, so changing the fuel changes cost and emissions at once.
fuel.sourcingHelp: Where the fuel comes from: bought at a market price, or produced in a plant you finance — then the plant's capital and running costs replace the purchase price. Build here derives those plant costs from a site evaluated on the map.
fuel.priceHelp: What one tonne of this fuel costs to buy. The yearly fuel bill is this price times consumption, so on most corridors it is one of the biggest levers.
fuel.combustionEfHelp: Tonnes of CO₂ released by burning one tonne of this fuel — a physical property of its chemistry. It drives the emissions bill and any carbon price on it.
fuel.lhvHelp: The energy in one tonne of this fuel (lower heating value). A fuel with less energy per tonne needs more tonnes for the same voyage — the main reason green fuels weigh more than the oil they replace.
fuel.prodCapexHelp: The one-off cost of building the production plant, when this fuel is produced rather than bought. Zero when purchasing.
fuel.prodOpexHelp: The yearly cost of running that production plant. Zero when purchasing.

port.fossilNote: Fossil benchmarks assume existing infrastructure: CAPEX 0, OPEX at 30% of a new green facility.
port.storageCapexHelp: The one-off cost of the tanks and loading equipment this fuel needs at the port. Ammonia and hydrogen need refrigerated or pressurised storage, which is why the green side usually costs more here.
port.storageOpexHelp: The yearly cost of running that port storage.
port.bargeCapexHelp: The one-off cost of the bunkering barges that carry fuel from the terminal to the ship.
port.bargeOpexHelp: The yearly cost of running those barges.

regulation.phaseNote: Phase-in applied automatically: 40% in 2024, 70% in 2025, 100% from 2026.
regulation.targetNote: Target reduction applied automatically: 2% from 2025 stepping to 80% by 2050.
regulation.usProduced: Green fuel produced in the US
regulation.escalationHelp: 0 = flat nominal price — at 2% inflation that is a falling real price. Set equal to inflation to hold the real carbon price constant; the IMO framework’s remedial prices escalate by construction.
regulation.imoRewardHelp: The reward for zero/near-zero fuel surplus below the direct-compliance target. Genuinely undetermined at source — default 0; the surplus balance is reported in tonnes regardless.
regulation.imoNote: Draft MEPC 83 structure (approved Apr 2025; adoption targeted MEPC 85, Oct 2026 — provisional): attained WTW fuel intensity vs two reduction ladders against the 93.3 gCO2eq/MJ 2008 reference; deficits priced $100/t (tier 1, direct→base band) and $380/t (tier 2, beyond base). Ladders agreed 2028–2035 and held flat beyond; tier prices established 2028–2030.
regulation.imoNotParam: Not parameterised: the pinned reference bundle has no IMO Net-Zero rows — the module reports nothing rather than silently computing zero.
regulation.finGreenRateHelp: Concessional green rates are a negotiation outcome, not a market observable - there is no benchmark to defer to. Green/transition loan margins typically land 0.5-2.5pp below a comparable conventional facility; type the rate your deal reflects.
regulation.finBaseRateHelp: What the green capital would pay without the green label. Initialised to the corridor discount rate; the SAVING is outstanding debt x (base - green).
regulation.finDebtShareHelp: Share of the green capital program that is debt-financed. The interest effect applies only to this share.
regulation.finTenorHelp: Years over which the debt runs. Amortizing repays principal straight-line over the tenor; bullet carries the full balance to maturity.
regulation.finStructureHelp: Planning-level loan shapes, not term sheets: amortizing = straight-line principal; bullet = full balance to maturity. The MMMCZCS study's ~$250m benefit sits between the two on the reference corridor ($196m amortizing, $313m bullet).
regulation.finNote: An explicit interest line on debt-financed green capital - a saving when the green rate is lower, a premium when higher. Deliberately NOT a lower discount rate, which would make future costs LARGER in present value.
regulation.phasingYearsHelp: Years over which each side's CAPEX is drawn down. One year reproduces the up-front charge exactly; later capital discounts more, so its present value falls.
regulation.phasingNote: Spreads each side's CAPEX over the first N years by explicit shares. Shares must sum to 1 - nothing is silently normalised. The green financing drawdown follows the same schedule.
regulation.frameworkHelp: Which framework's emission accounting the corridor's fuel intensities derive from. The same physical fuel carries different official values under the two frameworks (FuelEU bins residual fuels by ISO 8217 viscosity at WtT 13.5; the IMO bins by sulphur at 16.8/14.1) and each fixes its own GWP set. Default: FuelEU. The FuelEU and IMO compliance modules each price with their OWN framework regardless of this selection - it governs the reported intensities, abatement and the self-designed CO2 price.
regulation.frameworkNote: Fuel factors derive from the fuel-emissions dataset {dataset}: certified pathway + N2O slip + pilot blend on the green side, framework-resolved rows on the fossil side. Effective values appear in the Energy tab; explicit overrides there still win.
regulation.frameworkLegacyNote: This scenario runs the legacy workbook factors (pre-v6). Pick a framework to upgrade it to the refined method.
regulation.wtpHelp: What the cargo owner will fund per tonne of CO2e abated. Does NOT reduce the corridor cost - it splits the incremental cost into a customer share and the public funding that remains. 0 = none.
regulation.etsScopeHelp: 1.0 for a voyage between two EEA ports; 0.5 for a voyage between an EEA and a third-country port. The Directive counts 100% of emissions on intra-EEA voyages and 50% on voyages with one leg outside the EEA. Emissions at berth in an EEA port are chargeable at 100% regardless — not modelled separately, so a corridor of extra-EEA voyages understates slightly.
regulation.emissionsBasisHelp: Combustion counts only what leaves the ship's funnel; well-to-wake adds producing and transporting the fuel. Well-to-wake is what EU regulation prices, and the default.
regulation.rateBasisHelp: Whether the discount rate is nominal (costs grow with inflation before discounting) or real (inflation netted out). Keep it consistent with how your WACC was quoted.
regulation.etsIncludeHelp: Adds the EU carbon market: every tonne of CO₂ pays the allowance price over the covered share of the route. Fossil emissions cost money, which works in the green side's favour.
regulation.euaHelp: The price of one EU emission allowance — what emitting one tonne of CO₂ costs under the ETS.
regulation.eurUsdHelp: The exchange rate converting the euro-denominated EU schemes into the model's dollars.
regulation.fuelEuIncludeHelp: Adds FuelEU Maritime: a penalty when the energy used is more carbon-intensive than the falling EU target. Fossil fuel misses the target and pays; compliant green fuel can even earn a tradable credit.
regulation.penaltyHelp: The penalty per tonne of VLSFO-equivalent energy that misses the FuelEU intensity target. The regulation fixes it at €2,400; it is editable so you can test other levels.
regulation.fuelEuScopeHelp: The share of the route's energy FuelEU covers: 1.0 for voyages within the EEA, 0.5 for voyages into or out of it. A property of the route, not a preference.
regulation.vlsfoHelp: The energy assumed in one tonne of VLSFO — the unit the penalty is quoted in. A regulatory constant, shown rather than hidden.
regulation.baselineHelp: The reference carbon intensity the FuelEU targets are cut from (91.16 gCO₂e/MJ, the 2020 fleet average). Each target year is a percentage below this number.
regulation.iraIncludeHelp: Adds the US 45Z clean fuel credit: a payment per gallon-equivalent of qualifying fuel — available only while the fuel is produced in the United States.
regulation.usProducedHelp: 45Z only pays for fuel made in the United States. Switched off, the corridor's fuel does not qualify and the credit is zero.
regulation.rateHelp: The credit paid per gallon-equivalent of qualifying clean fuel. $1 is the statutory base rate.
regulation.imoIncludeHelp: Adds the IMO's net-zero framework: a global price on emissions above the IMO intensity target, with an optional reward for zero-emission fuels.
regulation.imoScopeHelp: The share of the route's emissions the IMO framework covers. It applies globally, so 1.0 is the normal value.
regulation.finToggleHelp: Models the green side borrowing at its own interest rate — cheaper green debt becomes an explicit yearly saving line in the comparison, never a changed discount rate.
regulation.phasingToggleHelp: Spreads each side's capital spending over the first years instead of all at once. Later spending counts for less after discounting, so phasing lowers the present cost of capital.
regulation.phasingWeightHelp: The share of this side's total capital spent in this year. The years together must sum to exactly 1.
regulation.selfIncludeHelp: A support scheme you design yourself — a carbon price, per-kilogram support, capital or operating subsidies, or a lump sum — to find what level of support closes the gap.
regulation.co2PriceHelp: Your scheme's price per tonne of CO₂, charged on fossil emissions — a carbon tax at whatever level you choose.
regulation.supportHelp: Support paid per kilogram of green fuel — the shape of production incentives such as hydrogen auction premiums.
regulation.capexSupportHelp: The fraction of green capital costs covered by grants: 0.3 means 30% of the ships and plant are paid by the scheme.
regulation.opexSupportHelp: The fraction of green operating costs covered each year.
regulation.otherHelp: Any other yearly support, in dollars — port-fee waivers, tax breaks, a grant spread over the years. The catch-all for money that fits no other box.

results.heading: Results
results.gapHelp: Green cost minus fossil cost — the gap a green premium or public support would need to close.
results.waterfall: Breakdown of total cost of the green corridor (PV)
results.netReg: Net regulatory effect on the gap
results.bothBases: CO2 abated — combustion: {ttw} t · well-to-wake: {wtw} t
results.abatementNoteEts: The premium per tonne of CO2 avoided, next to the EU ETS allowance price you entered — the market’s going rate for a tonne.
results.abatementNoteSelf: The premium per tonne of CO2 avoided, next to your self-designed scheme’s carbon price — the rate this scenario actually charges.
results.abatementNoteImo: The premium per tonne of CO2 avoided, next to the IMO Net-Zero remedial price that applies in this scenario.
results.abatementNoteNone: No carbon price is active in this scenario — enable EU ETS, the self-designed scheme or the IMO framework to compare against one.
results.imoNotParam: IMO Net-Zero: not parameterised in the pinned reference bundle.
results.annualYear1Caption: Year 1 carries {capital} of green capital, charged in full up front — year 1 alone is {share}% of the lifetime gap.
results.annualPhasedCaption: Year 1 carries {capital} of green capital under the deployment schedule — year 1 alone is {share}% of the lifetime gap.
results.energyParityNote: The two sides deliver {pct}% different energy ({side} carries more), so the abated tonnes compare unequal transport work. Nothing has been rescaled — check whether one side's fuel use was overridden alone.
results.wfFootnote: * excludes every regulatory instrument - hover the Regulations bar for the breakdown, including schemes that do not apply here
results.waterfallPerTonne: Breakdown of abatement cost per tonne of CO2
results.probIntro: The incremental cost gap shown as a range rather than a single number.
results.probCaveat: Illustrative only — an even ±30% spread around each calculated value, not a modelled uncertainty. Every figure below is the central value times a fixed factor.
results.tornadoIntro: Each bar re-runs the whole model at the two ends of a researched range. Bar length is what that uncertainty is worth on THIS scenario — a wide range on a field the corridor barely uses moves nothing.
results.tornadoCaveat: Ranges are researched and cited; the model supplies the leverage. Inputs with no declared range are absent from this chart entirely — absence means nobody has stated a range, not that the input does not matter.

buildHere.chip: cell {cell} · LCOH ${lcoh}/kg ({rate}%) · synthesis {nameplate} kt/yr, scale ×{scale} · {km} km to port
buildHere.configNote: Each component is a derived seed from the evaluation — edit any one to override just that line (the derived value stays as the restorable benchmark). Typical use: accept the map’s hydrogen cost, replace the synthesis plant with your EPC quote.
buildHere.pickOnMap: No evaluated site yet — click a coloured hex on the map, open the cell, choose “Use as corridor fuel site”, adjust any assumptions, press Calculate, then hand the result back.
buildHere.repickNote: Pick any other hex on the map to move the site.
buildHere.displayOnly: (display figure — the corridor discounts the raw CAPEX/OPEX)
buildHere.sizingLine: Plant sized to corridor demand: {demand} t/yr × {margin} margin = {nameplate} t/yr nameplate ({surplus} t/yr surplus — reported, never apportioned).
buildHere.rateWarning: The LCOH evaluation ran at {lcohRate}% while the corridor discounts at {corridorRate}%. The LCOH-internal rate is display-only — the corridor applies its own rate to these CAPEX/OPEX lines — but the site’s levelized $/kg was computed at the other rate.
buildHere.engineMoved: Evaluated with LCOH engine {evaluated}; current is {current}. Stored values still apply — re-run the evaluation on the map to refresh them (never automatic).
buildHere.sumLine: Production CAPEX = ${capex}m · production OPEX = ${opex}m/yr — the lines the corridor engine consumes.
buildHere.firmingHeadline: This site runs {evaluated}% of the year; the carrier's synthesis loop needs {required}%. The shortfall is priced below — a plant fed by unbuffered daytime power could not make this fuel.
buildHere.bandNote: A screening estimate, not a quote — the range comes from the four sourced drivers. Most of the spread is

componentHelp.h2Capital: The one-off cost of the electrolysis plant and its power supply at this site, derived from the map evaluation. Override it to test your own quote.
componentHelp.synthCapital: The one-off cost of the synthesis step that turns hydrogen into the shipping fuel — the ammonia or methanol plant.
componentHelp.h2Operating: The yearly cost of running the hydrogen plant, dominated by electricity.
componentHelp.synthOperating: The yearly cost of running the synthesis plant.
componentHelp.logisticsOperating: The yearly cost of moving the finished fuel from the plant to the port.

scenarioBar.name: Scenario name
scenarioBar.resetConfirm: Start a new corridor? This clears the current draft.
scenarioBar.loadedMigrated: Loaded (payload migrated from schema v{from} and re-evaluated with the current engine)
scenarioBar.loadedNewerEngine: Loaded — saved with engine {saved}; results shown are re-evaluated with the current engine

corridor.legacyBanner: Legacy accounting loaded: this scenario charges the merchant fuel price AND production CAPEX/O&M — production cost is counted twice. Preserved verbatim for comparison with the original source; new scenarios cannot select this mode.
corridor.vesselBurnBanner: Fuel use was stated directly in this scenario, from the vessel table's flat annual figure. Your numbers are unchanged — the burn is now an explicit override you can see and edit. It is worth a look: green {greenFrozen} t/vessel/yr (this corridor's distance implies {greenDerived}), fossil {fossilFrozen} t (implies {fossilDerived}). The table figure is a fleet average over an unstated trade pattern, so it does not reflect how far these ships actually steam.
corridor.vesselBurnParity: The two sides also deliver {pct}% different energy, so the abated tonnes compare unequal transport work.

shared.notFound: No shared scenario for this link (it may have been revoked).
shared.staleBanner: Saved with engine {engine} / bundle {bundle}; current is {currentEngine} / {currentBundle}. Newer model available — recompute?
shared.recomputedNote: Showing results recomputed with the current engine — the stored version is unchanged.

projects.heading: Projects
projects.intro: Select a project to work on - or create a new one. The input tabs unlock once a project is open. You start with four views of the same Chilean corridor - the shipped default, the report's own accounting, the current model, and in-model benchmarks only - plus an empty Simplified starter.
projects.newProjectNote: A new project starts from a blank corridor - generic route, benchmark costs, every scheme off. Simplified can be upgraded to Standard later; the upgrade is permanent.
projects.discardConfirm: Discard unsaved changes to "{name}"? Opening another project replaces the working copy.
projects.currentSavedNote: Changes in the input tabs are not stored until you save.
projects.currentDraftNote: This draft lives in your browser only. Save it to keep it in your account and share it.
projects.emptyBody: The corridor you are working on is kept as a local draft. Save it as a project to keep it in your account, open it from any browser and share a read-only link.
projects.staleTitle: Saved with engine {saved}; the current engine is {current}. Opening it recomputes live and the difference is announced.
projects.footnote: Deleting a project is permanent. Share links are read-only and can be revoked at any time.

provenance.consumption: distance x 2 x roundtrips x vessel GJ/nm / fuel LHV (distance mode); vessel-table benchmark otherwise
provenance.vesselCapexGreen: vessel-type CAPEX x (1 + the fuel's vessel CAPEX premium)
provenance.portFossil: existing-infrastructure rule: CAPEX 0, OPEX at 30% of a new green facility
provenance.priceZero: no merchant price under build sourcing - production cost is CAPEX + O&M
